purpose: Make the frozen Legacy shared RK candidate closure, group commit and membership validation executable without linking Legacy into the main build.

provenance.notes: An external C++17 harness was compiled against a clean extraction of the frozen archive with w64devkit GCC 16.2.0 and run twice. The main build consumes pinned traces, a 50-digit Decimal derivation and an independent C++17 joint-state probe with no Legacy dependency.

expected_facts.claim: Mass and position derivatives read one joint candidate vector at all four RK stages, producing mass=8 and position=9 after dt=1.
expected_facts.tolerance_policy: Stage identity, time, event order and multiplicity are exact; synthetic scalar fields use absolute tolerance 1e-12.

expected_facts.claim: The joint candidate commits once and distributes mass=8 and position=9 to both declared members.
expected_facts.tolerance_policy: Commit event identity and count are exact; synthetic scalar fields use absolute tolerance 1e-12.

expected_facts.claim: Every scope member must be registered, may belong to only one continuous scope and is bound by stable member identity independently of declaration or packed storage order.
expected_facts.tolerance_policy: Membership identity plus valid, unregistered and duplicate-ownership outcomes are exact; declaration and packed storage order are excluded after identity binding.

expected_facts.claim: The trace is tied to the frozen archive, group interface, RK4 implementation, simulator, passing runtime test, capture harness and canonical environment evidence.
expected_facts.tolerance_policy: Paths, byte counts and SHA-256 values are exact.

acceptance: Verifies frozen source, environment, harness and runtime-test identities before comparing behavior
Two raw Legacy captures normalize to one semantic stage and commit trace after excluding only rerun_index
Independent 50-digit Decimal and C++17 joint-state RK4 implementations agree with every Legacy stage and final member value
Rejects split snapshot closure, an unregistered member and duplicate scope ownership
Accepts member declaration and packed storage reordering after stable identity binding
The accepted disposition preserves shared candidates, one scope commit and unique identity-bound membership while retiring the Legacy group surface and manual vector packing
